records.deidentified_narrative: on june 8, 2018 i was assigned a follow up investigation involving a hit and run crash that occurred on june 3, 2018. on june 9, 2018 i received information from liberty eylau isd police officer carl valentine who is a courtesy officer for the lakeridge apartments, advising that he observed the suspect vehicle on the property and stated that it was a red ford edge bearing a texas lp of dcc 1268. valentine stated that the driver does not live on the property but visits an apartment on the property. i ran the license plate through nlets and obtained the owners information. the registered owners of the 2007 red ford edge were basil murrain and lashonta simpson. i was able to obtain information on basil murrain and lashonta simpson from an old landlord. on june 19, 2018 i made contact with murrain via telephone and informed him of the reason i was calling. i asked murrain if he drove the red 2007 ford edge and he stated he did. murrain advised that he was at lakeridge apartments on the day of the crash but denied striking a pedestrian. murrain informed me that as he was exiting the parking lot he observed a kid run into a parked vehicle and fall down. i obtained the video footage from officer butts and reviewed it. in the video i observed a red suv pull through the parking lot as harmen started to run across the parking lot. as the suv passes i observed harmen on the ground. there were no parked vehicles in the path of harmen. i made contact with shalethe williams who is the mother of deundrae harman. williams informed me that she does wish to pursue charges on murrain because he did not attempt to help her son. williams informed [medical facility] by life net but only suffered minor bruising in his leg.

records.public_safe_text: the driver of unit 1 was traveling through the parking lot of her apartment complex, from east to west, across the parking lot to approach her designated building's parking space. the driver of unit 1's desired parking space was the 5th parking spot from the east end of the row. as the driver of unit 1 approached the parking lot row, she could she that a vehicle was parked right next to her desired parking spot in space number 4 from the east, tx lp: [identifier], white kia optima, owner: frank, (817) 779-1086. the driver of unit 1 also noticed that the spot next to vehicle tx lp: [identifier], space 5, was [roadway], there was no vehicle occupying the space, no rope or tape blocking the space off and no sign posted for no parking. as she began to pull into the space, the driver of unit 1 suddenly heard a loud scream, so she immediately stopped her vehicle. as she got out, she realized that the pedestrian was laying down in the parking space to sleep and his hand had been struck by unit 1's front right tire. the driver of unit 1 said that she could not see the pedestrian sleeping in the parking spot because her view was blocked by the kia optima, parked in space 4, which was concealing the sleeping pedestrian. the driver of unit 1 called 911 and sat with the pedestrian until an ambulance arrived. the driver of unit 1 also stated that she spoke with frank, the owner of the white kia optima, and frank stated that the pedestrian was laying down asleep in his parking spot when he arrived earlier in the day. frank also added that he needed to honk his horn twice to get the pedestrian to move out of the spot. once frank had parked, the pedestrian lied down again, this time next to frank's vehicle, with his hand in space number 5.

records.public_safe_text: on may 24, 2018 at approximately 0900 hours. pedestrian identified as leo donald lamontagne was walking north in approximately the 2700 block of rr 336. a 2011 harley davidson motorcycle was also traveling north on rr 336 in the 2700 block, the operator was identified as richard lee kennedy. the pedestrian walked in front of the motorcycle and was struck. a witness to the crash identified as bella a rubio , states that she was driving south on rr 336 . the witness states that she passed the pedestrian, then she passed the motorcycle . witness states that the pedestrian was walking north along the [roadway]. she looked in her rear view mirror and saw the motorcycle strike the pedestrian, then the pedestrian flew into the air. the witness turned around and stopped, she talked to the pedestrian and then notified the passengers of another vehicle that had stopped, that there was a man (motorcycle operator) lying along the [roadway] in the grass. witness then talked to a male cutting grass along a fence and told him to notify ""911"". (written statement of witness attached to report). the pedestrian was [roadway] on his back, with his head facing south. a written statement that was received by fax from ""[medical facility] in san antonio from the operator of motorcycle states . the operator was north bound on rr 336. the operator saw the pedestrian and slowed down to approximately 30 mph. he then moved over to [roadway]. then the pedestrian walked in front of the motorcycle. operator states that he could not stop ,slowdown, he was already committed. he then struck the pedestrian. the operator and motorcycle then went to the left, and the motorcycle and driver operator traveled approximately 40 [roadway]. the operator then fell off the motorcycle on the west side of rr 336 next to mm 480, in the grass. the motorcycle without a driver operator traveled approximately 20 feet then stopped entangled in a bob wire fence. the operator was lying in the grass on the west side of the roadway, on his back, with helmet still on. deputy douthit faxed a blank statement to ""[medical facility] on june 6, 2018 at approximately 10:15 hours. for pedestrian to fill out, then fax back. deputy douthit made contact by phone several times with next of kin that a statement was needed for the report. no response at this time.

records.deidentified_narrative: driver of unit 1, which was towing a boat & trailer (unit 2), had gotten into a verbal argument with a group of pedestrians in the parking lot. witnesses (caleb duncan [phone], daisy villalobos [phone] and caleb duncan [phone]) said the driver of unit 1 made a ""loop"" around the group of pedestrians and as it did so, the left side of unit 2 struck unit 4. two pedestrians who were standing next to unit 4 on the driver's side, were stuck by unit 4 because the force of the impact between unit 2 and unit 4 caused unit 4 to be moved/dragged to where the two pedestrians (unit 5 and unit 6) were standing. witnesses said unit 1 & 2 then drove off. daisy was able to show officers pictures of the license plates of unit 1 & unit 2. unit 5 (jason rainey) was treated at the scene by [medical facility] by a family member. unit 6 (trey cochran) said the upper part of unit 4 struck him on his head above his right eye, where some minor bruising was observed. the license plates that daisy photographed ([identifier] & 028357k) were run and the return showed the owner of unit 1 & unit 2 to be brandon barrick, [roadway], arlington tx. daisy also showed officers a picture of the driver of unit 1. he appeared to be a w/m, large frame, bald head. daisy said he had a goatee on his face. officers went to [roadway] and made contact with brandon barrick as he was standing in his front yard. he matched the picture that daisy had shown officers earlier. parked in his driveway was his gray 2011 dodge pickup truck (txlp [identifier]) and his boat trailer (txlp 028357k). initially, brandon barrick said there was no altercation in the park parking lot, but later changed his story and said there was a verbal altercation between him and a group of teenagers who surrounded his vehicle. brandon said to avoid any further problems, he drove away from the group of individuals, but said that neither his pickup truck nor his trailer hit any parked vehicles. i noticed what appeared to be fresh damage to the left side wheel area of the blue boat trailer and noticed a small section of red paint transfer in the damage area of the trailer fender. unit 4 is a red chevrolet pickup truck. the damage to the trailer and the red paint transfer to the trailer appear to match what witnesses told officers. brandon barrick claimed the damage to his boat trailer was old, but that doesn't appear to be the case. the driver of unit 3 said his vehicle was parked to the right of unit 4 and said that he observed his vehicle ""move"" during the incident and claimed that his vehicle was struck by either unit 1 or unit 2 in the rfq area. at this time, officers could not see any damage to his vehicle. it is possible that the damage to unit 3 is so minor it is difficult to see in low light conditions. [date] after further investigation, it was determined that unit 1 was driven by brandon barrick and the damage to unit 2 correlated to the damage observed on unit 4, which appeared to be over $200.
